_comment: The COMMITTED inventory of the 1985 standard's paragraphs whose body carries an ascending '(n)' list under a
heading that names no rule block (kb/Work PB4886): the 1985 arm of the 2023 arm's content-keyed scan (kb/Work
PB29, spec-unharvested-rule-blocks.json, the same shape and the same test), keyed by CITATION since the base text
(Appendix A) and Amendment 1 (Section A) both have an A.2.1. extract_rule_catalog.py --edition 1985 measures every
paragraph of every section and appendix and fails --check on a paragraph measured and not declared here, one
declared and no longer measured, or an ordinal count that moved. disposition 'rules' ADMITS the paragraph to the
denominator as a rule block of `kind` (admitted_kinds: one kind, a per-item map, a per-sub-list map); 'not-rules'
records why its list is no requirement; 'pending' is a worklist entry, never a decision. The test is the 1985
standard's own: IV.3.1 (a syntax rule defines 'the order in which words or elements are arranged' and may 'impose
restrictions on individual words or elements') and IV.3.2 (a general rule defines 'the meaning or relationship of
meanings' and 'the effect that it has on either execution or compilation'), read with the 2023 manifest's
dispositions of the same text. Shape is no proof either way: read the paragraph.

§1985:II.3.2.4.2.title: Logical Subdivisions of a Report
§1985:II.3.2.4.2.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'The occurrence of a control break causes the following sequence of events to take place'. The three items fix the order in which the report writer control system presents the control footing, control heading and detail groups at a control break: what the object program does, normative. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:II.4.2.title: INITIAL VALUES OF TABLES
§1985:II.4.2.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'In the Working-Storage Section, initial values of elements within tables are specified in one of the following ways'. Items 1 and 2 each carry a prohibition ('must not contain VALUE clauses') on the entries a table's initialization may be written with, and item 3 permits VALUE clauses on selected elements: restrictions and permissions on what is written, normative. Kind SR by IV.3.1 of the 1985 standard: the items restrict how words or elements may be written or where they may appear.

§1985:II.6.2.3.title: Name Resolution
§1985:II.6.2.3.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'Consider the situation when program A contains program B which itself contains program C ...'. The five items are a WORKED EXAMPLE on hypothetical programs A, B and C and the name DUPLICATE-NAME; the rules they illustrate are X.1.3.8.2 'Conventions for Condition-Names, Data-Names, File-Names, Record-Names, and Report-Names', admitted here as its own rows. An example states no requirement of its own.

§1985:II.6.4.1.2.title: Scope of the CALL Statement
§1985:II.6.4.1.2.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'In the following, the calling program may or may not possess any of the program attributes ...'. The four items state which programs a CALL statement may name ('A calling program may call a program which neither possesses the common attribute nor is separately compiled if, and only if, ...'): the scope a program-name has in a CALL, normative, as the 2023 manifest admits 8.4.6.3 'Scope of program-names' SR. Kind SR by IV.3.1 of the 1985 standard: the items restrict how words or elements may be written or where they may appear.

§1985:II.6.4.1.3.title: Scope of Names of Programs
§1985:II.6.4.1.3.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'The name DUPLICATE-NAME has also been specified for a separately compiled program.' The four items are a WORKED EXAMPLE of which program a call of DUPLICATE-NAME activates in a figure's nesting; the rules it illustrates are II.6.4.1.2 and X.1.3.8.1, admitted as their own rows.

§1985:II.6.4.3.title: Sharing Data
§1985:II.6.4.3.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'Two programs in a run unit may reference common data in the following circumstances'. The three items restate X.1.3.6 'Sharing Data' word for word (adding only a 'See page II-19' reference); that paragraph, in its module and with its level-2 box, is admitted, and a second row for the same requirement would count it twice.

§1985:II.6.4.4.title: Sharing Files
§1985:II.6.4.4.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'Two programs in a run unit may reference common file connectors in the following circumstances'. The two items restate X.1.3.7 'Sharing Files' word for word; that paragraph is admitted, and a second row would count the requirement twice.

§1985:II.6.5.1.title: Transfer of Control
§1985:II.6.5.1.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'There are four methods of transferring control within a program'. The items are bare names of statements and procedures (a GO TO statement, a PERFORM statement, ...): an index of the constructs whose own general rules transfer control, as the 2023 manifest records 10.3.

§1985:II.7.1.title: THE MESSAGE CONTROL SYSTEM
§1985:II.7.1.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'The primary functions of the message control system are the following'. The items describe what the message control system, a facility outside the COBOL implementation, does (line discipline, device-dependent tasks); they bind neither a program nor the implementation.

§1985:II.7.3.title: RELATIONSHIP OF THE COBOL PROGRAM TO THE MESSAGE CONTROL SYSTEM AND COMMUNICATION DEVICES
§1985:II.7.3.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-ins: 'There are two such interfaces', 'The COBOL source program uses three statements to control the interface with the message control system', 'uses two statements to control the interface between the message control system and the communication devices'. The three lists name the interfaces and the statements (RECEIVE, SEND, ACCEPT MESSAGE COUNT, ENABLE, DISABLE), each specified by its own rules in Section XIV: an index.

§1985:II.7.3.1.1.title: Scheduled Initiation of the COBOL Object Program
§1985:II.7.3.1.1.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'the COBOL program can use three methods to determine what messages, if any, are available'. The items name the statements a program may use (ACCEPT MESSAGE COUNT, RECEIVE with and without NO DATA), each specified in Section XIV: an index of techniques, no requirement.

§1985:II.7.3.1.3.title: Determining the Method of Scheduling
§1985:II.7.3.1.3.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'the following is one technique that may be used'. The standard itself calls the list ONE TECHNIQUE a program may use; it imposes nothing.

§1985:II.7.5.1.title: Independent Enqueueing and Dequeueing
§1985:II.7.5.1.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'the message control system enqueues the message ...'. The two items describe when the message control system, outside the implementation, holds output messages in a queue (the queue disabled, the destination slower); descriptive.

§1985:II.7.5.4.title: Queue Hierarchy
§1985:II.7.5.4.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-ins: 'Let us assume that the message control system is operating under the following queueing algorithm' and 'The following examples illustrate the effect of the above algorithms'. A hypothetical algorithm and its worked examples, by the text's own words.

§1985:III.2.title: DEFINITIONS
§1985:III.2.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). The glossary's definitions ('At End Condition. A condition caused: (1) ...', 'Qualifier', 'Text Word'): terms whose rules are stated where each construct is specified (the READ, RETURN and SEARCH general rules for the at end condition), as the 2023 catalog carries no row for a term of clause 3.

§1985:IV.4.2.1.title: Separators
§1985:IV.4.2.1.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'A separator is a character or two contiguous characters formed according to the following rules': each a restriction on how source text is written (where a space, a quotation mark or a pseudo-text delimiter may stand). The amendments name them 'rule 4' and 'rule 5' (X3.23a-1989 IV-4, X3.23b-1993 IV-4 and IV-5), and the 2023 manifest admits 8.3.5 Separators SR. Kind SR by IV.3.1 of the 1985 standard: the items restrict how words or elements may be written or where they may appear.

§1985:IV.4.2.2.1.title: COBOL Words
§1985:IV.4.2.2.1.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-09 (kb/Work PB5045: Amendment 1's Addendum 1 adds the list, row IV-5, applied in place). Lead-in: 'Within a source program the following apply'. Item 1 states which COBOL words form disjoint or intersecting sets for all words but LENGTH, RANDOM and SUM, item 2 that those three are reserved words and function-names and never user-defined words or system-names: each restricts which word a program may write where. Kind SR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define or clarify how words may be arranged, as IV.4.2.1 Separators is admitted.

§1985:IV.4.2.2.1.3.title: Reserved Words
§1985:IV.4.2.2.1.3.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'Reserved words satisfy the following conditions'. The four items state properties of the standard's OWN list of reserved words (no reserved word begins with a digit, X, Y or Z; none is one letter; ...): a description of a list the standard fixes (IV-45, COBOL Reserved Words), which binds no program and no implementation. What binds a program is the paragraph's lead sentence ('must not appear in the programs as user-defined words'), which is not a numbered item.

§1985:IV.4.2.2.1.3.1.title: Required Words
§1985:IV.4.2.2.1.3.1.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'Required words are of two types'. Key words (uppercase and underlined in a format) and special character words (the arithmetic operators and relation characters) are the words a format requires to be written, as the 2023 manifest admits 8.3.2.4.2 'Required words' SR. Kind SR by IV.3.1 of the 1985 standard: the items restrict how words or elements may be written or where they may appear.

§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.2.title: Numeric Literals
§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.2.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'The rules for the formation of numeric literals are as follows' (the body calls them rules). Items 1-3 restrict the literal's written form (at least one digit, at most one sign and leftmost, at most one decimal point and not rightmost) ⇒ SR by IV.3.1; item 4 states its value and category ('The value of a numeric literal is the algebraic quantity represented') ⇒ GR by IV.3.2. The 2023 manifest types 8.3.3.3.2 the same way.

§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3.title: Figurative Constant Values
§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Three lists. List 1 (the figurative constant values and the words that reference them: 'Represents the numeric value 0 ...') and list 2 ('the length of the string is determined by the compiler from context according to the following rules') define the value and the length of each figurative constant ⇒ GR by IV.3.2. List 3 ('A figurative constant may be used whenever literal appears in a format with the following exceptions') restricts where a figurative constant may be written (only ZERO where a numeric literal is required, ALL literal with a numeric item an obsolete element, ALL redundant otherwise) ⇒ SR by IV.3.1.

§1985:IV.4.3.1.1.title: Physical Aspects of a File
§1985:IV.4.3.1.1.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'The physical aspects of a file describe the data as it appears on the input or output media and include such features as'. Illustrative and non-exhaustive ('include such features as'), two bare noun phrases; the 2023 manifest records the same text, 9.1.1, as not rules.

§1985:IV.4.3.2.1.title: Level-Numbers
§1985:IV.4.3.2.1.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'Three types of entries exist for which there is no true concept of level. These are'. The items fix which entries (RENAMES, noncontiguous items, condition-names) have no level in the hierarchy, a definition the level-number rules depend on, as the 2023 manifest admits 8.5.1.3.2 'Level-numbers' GR. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:IV.4.3.6.title: Standard Alignment Rules
§1985:IV.4.3.6.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). 'Standard Alignment Rules': 'The standard rules for positioning data within an elementary item depend on the category of the receiving item'; how data is positioned in a receiving item, the effect of a move. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:IV.4.3.7.title: Item Alignment for Increased Object-Code Efficiency
§1985:IV.4.3.7.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'Synchronization can be accomplished in two ways'. The two ways (the SYNCHRONIZED clause, and organizing data on natural boundaries) define the facility, as the 2023 manifest admits 8.5.1.6.4 'Item alignment for increased object-code efficiency' GR. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:IV.4.3.8.1.title: Qualification
§1985:IV.4.3.8.1.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Two lists: 'Every user-defined name explicitly referenced in a COBOL source program must be uniquely referenced because either' and 'The rules for qualification are as follows' (the body calls them rules): what must be written to reference a name uniquely, which qualifiers are allowed, and the names that must be qualified each time they are referenced. The 2023 manifest admits the same rules, 8.4.2.2.1, SR. Kind SR by IV.3.1 of the 1985 standard: the items restrict how words or elements may be written or where they may appear.

§1985:IV.4.4.title: EXPLICIT AND IMPLICIT SPECIFICATIONS
§1985:IV.4.4.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'There are four types of explicit and implicit specifications that occur in COBOL source programs'. The items are the titles of the four subparagraphs IV.4.4.1 to IV.4.4.4 that follow: a table of contents.

§1985:IV.4.4.2.title: Explicit and Implicit Transfers of Control
§1985:IV.4.4.2.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Two lists: 'COBOL provides the following types of implicit control flow alterations' and 'There is no next executable statement when the program contains no Procedure Division or following'. Both define where control goes at execution, as the 2023 manifest admits 14.6.3 'Explicit and implicit transfers of control' GR. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:IV.4.4.4.title: Explicit and Implicit Scope Terminators
§1985:IV.4.4.4.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'The implicit scope terminators are the following'. The items define what terminates a statement's scope, as the 2023 manifest admits 14.5.3.3 'Implicit scope termination' GR. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:IV.6.4.2.1.1.title: Definition of Conditional Statement
§1985:IV.6.4.2.1.1.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'A conditional statement is one of the following'. The items define the category, which the rules on imperative and conditional statements turn on (where an imperative statement is required, these may not stand), a definitional list as the 2023 manifest admits 4.2.10. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:IV.6.4.2.1.1.1.title: Definition of Conditional Phrase
§1985:IV.6.4.2.1.1.1.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'A conditional phrase is one of the following'. As IV.6.4.2.1.1: the items define the category. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:VI.5.15.5.title: Condition-Name Rules
§1985:VI.5.15.5.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). 'Condition-Name Rules' of the VALUE clause continue its general rules (VI.5.15.4) by subject, as VI.5.15.6 does, whose rules X3.23a-1989 (VI-50) calls 'general rule 6'.

§1985:VI.5.15.6.title: Data Description Entries Other Than Condition-Names
§1985:VI.5.15.6.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). 'Data Description Entries Other Than Condition-Names' of the VALUE clause: X3.23a-1989's change on page VI-50 names its sixth rule 'general rule 6'.

§1985:VI.6.2.3.title: Formation and Evaluation Rules
§1985:VI.6.2.3.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). 'Formation and Evaluation Rules' of arithmetic expressions: rules 1, 2, 5 and 6 define the order and result of evaluation (GR by IV.3.2); rules 3 and 4 state which symbols may be written next to each other and how an expression may begin and end (SR by IV.3.1).

§1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2.title: Comparison of Nonnumeric Operands
§1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Two lists. List 1 ('If one of the operands is specified as numeric, it must be an integer data item or an integer literal and') defines how the numeric operand is treated (items 1 and 2, GR by IV.3.2) and forbids a noninteger numeric operand in the comparison (item 3, 'cannot be compared', SR by IV.3.1). List 2 ('There are two cases to consider: operands of equal size and operands of unequal size') defines the comparison (GR), as the 2023 manifest admits 8.8.4.2.7 'Comparison of alphanumeric operands' GR.

§1985:VI.6.3.1.1.3.title: Comparisons Involving Index-Names and/or Index Data Items
§1985:VI.6.3.1.1.3.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'Relation tests may be made only between'. Each item names a pair of operands and defines the comparison's result ('The result is the same as if the corresponding occurrence numbers were compared'), as the 2023 manifest admits 8.8.4.2.13 'Comparisons involving index-names or index data items' GR. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:VI.6.3.1.2.title: Class Condition
§1985:VI.6.3.1.2.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'The class of an operand is determined as follows': when an operand is numeric, alphabetic, alphabetic-lower, alphabetic-upper or in class-name-1, the class condition's value. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:VI.6.3.3.title: Abbreviated Combined Relation Conditions
§1985:VI.6.3.3.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Two lists of the boxed abbreviated combined relation conditions. List 1 states what may be OMITTED in writing an abbreviation (the subject, or the subject and relational operator) ⇒ SR by IV.3.1. List 2 ('The interpretation applied to the use of the word NOT in an abbreviated combined relation condition is as follows') defines its meaning ⇒ GR by IV.3.2.

§1985:VI.6.3.4.title: Order of Evaluation of Conditions
§1985:VI.6.3.4.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'the evaluation of the conditions within an entire complex condition begins at the left ... and proceeds according to the following rule recursively applied': the order of evaluation, as the 2023 manifest admits 8.8.4.13 'Order of evaluation of conditions' GR. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:VI.6.4.2.title: The ON SIZE ERROR Phrase
§1985:VI.6.4.2.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'The size error condition occurs under the following circumstances'. The items define when the size error condition exists (exponentiation, division by zero, overflow after radix point alignment), as the 2023 manifest admits 14.7.5 'SIZE ERROR phrase and size error condition' GR. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:VI.6.4.3.title: The CORRESPONDING Phrase
§1985:VI.6.4.3.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'A pair of data items, one from D1 and one from D2 correspond if the following conditions exist'. The items define correspondence (and what is ignored), as the 2023 manifest admits 14.7.6 'CORRESPONDING phrase' GR. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:VI.6.4.4.title: The Arithmetic Statements
§1985:VI.6.4.4.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'The arithmetic statements are the ADD, COMPUTE, DIVIDE, MULTIPLY, and SUBTRACT statements. They have several common features.' Item 1 (conversion and decimal point alignment are supplied) states an effect ⇒ GR by IV.3.2; item 2 ('The maximum size of each operand is 18 decimal digits. The composite of operands ... must not contain more than 18 decimal digits') restricts the operands that may be written ⇒ SR by IV.3.1, as the 2023 manifest types 14.7.7's item 2 SR.

§1985:VI.6.4.6.title: Multiple Results in Arithmetic Statements
§1985:VI.6.4.6.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-in: 'Such statements behave as though they had been written in the following way'. The items define the execution of an arithmetic statement with multiple results. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:VI.6.23.1.title: Function
§1985:VI.6.23.1.why: NOT-RULES 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). The Function paragraph of the SET statement: 'The SET statement establishes reference points ...', 'is also used to alter the status of external switches', 'the value of conditional variables'. A statement's Function paragraph summarizes what its general rules (VI.6.23.4) specify, and no other Function paragraph of the standard is a row; this one happens to number its sentences.

§1985:VII.1.3.5.title: I-O Status
§1985:VII.1.3.5.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Two lists: 'I-O status expresses one of the following conditions upon completion of the input-output operation' and 'The following is a list of the values placed in the I-O status for the previously named conditions'. They define each condition and the status values the implementation sets, as the 2023 manifest admits 9.1.13.2 to 9.1.13.11 GR. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:VIII.1.3.4.title: I-O Status
§1985:VIII.1.3.4.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). The relative I-O module's I-O status: as VII.1.3.5. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:VIII.1.3.5.title: The Invalid Key Condition
§1985:VIII.1.3.5.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). Lead-ins: 'If the invalid key condition exists after the execution of the input-output operation ..., the following actions occur in the order shown' and its converse. The items define the actions, as the 2023 manifest admits 9.1.14 'Invalid key condition' GR. Kind GR by IV.3.2 of the 1985 standard: the items define the meaning of an element or its effect at execution or compilation.

§1985:IX.1.3.4.title: I-O Status
§1985:IX.1.3.4.why: ADMITTED 2026-11-07 (kb/Work PB4886, the 1985 arm of the content-keyed scan; the 2023 manifest's test). The indexed I-O module's I-O status: as VII.1.3.5.
